The vote follows Fauci's decision last week to invoke his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination during testimony before the committee, declining to answer questions from Chairman Sen. Rand Paul. Fauci argued the hearing was politically motivated and said he was acting on the advice of counsel. If approved by the full Senate, the referral would be sent to the Department of Justice, which would decide whether to pursue criminal contempt charges. Such prosecutions are uncommon but have occurred in recent years, including the cases of Steve Bannon and Peter Navarro.

headline: Six months after the deadliest U.S. loss of the Iran War, Sen. Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) is demanding the Pentagon publicly release its investigation into the March 1 Iranian attack in Kuwait that killed six U.S. service members. In a letter obtained by CBS News, Baldwin called on U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) to provide Congress with the full 350+ page report, supporting documentation, and any classified reviews. She is also seeking answers about reported delays in medical care and force protection decisions before the attack. The push follows earlier CBS News reporting that survivors alleged intelligence warnings were ignored, the unit was not adequately fortified, and requests for additional medical supplies were denied. The Pentagon has completed its investigation and briefed families of the fallen, but has not yet publicly released its findings or assigned responsibility for any command decisions. At the same time, the Pentagon is likely weighing transparency against operational security. A public release could expose vulnerabilities in force protection, intelligence collection, medical response, or command procedures that Iran could study and exploit. Similar investigations are often released only in redacted form or classified versions for that reason.
